I need to define Service Principals to run workspace admin tasks in each workspace, as well as an SP in each workspace that can be provisioned with both “workspace admin” access and API credentials to the Workspace API. This will be used to query the API and can information on workspace configuration and entitlements.

Below is an excerpt from a conversation with Zach:

----

*Scott*

Hey, got a question for you:

I have code that uses the Databricks Python SDK to query the Workspace API. In order to that, it defaults to authenticating to the API using the identity of the Service Principal that's running the job; however, I could pass in different credentials (using DB secrets) if I wanted to. Whichever SP I use has to be permissioned with access to the API.

 Do you think it would make more sense to:

# Permission each global STL runner SP against the API for their particular workspace
# Create a specific SP for each workspace whose credentials I explicitly invoke to query the API
# Create a different SP other than the Global STL Runner to run these specific jobs
# Something else I haven't thought of

?

*Zach*

hmm. let me think about that. need to consider where the risk sits in each case under a breach. options 2 and 3 are the same under Keyera's current security requirements.

so its a decision between does the ETL runner SP get access to the API or does a separte SP

Ok so if we are going to follow the general pattern it will be a combination of 1 and 2.

First off there is a different SP runner for every source system. the global one is only used for gold. So you will have a {{SP Extraction Databricks | <workspace>}} service principal. That SP then has the ACLs for read access on the secret scope that stores the credentials for accessing the source application. The credentials would then be tied to a different databricks SP.

Now the second SP seems redundant b/c Databricks is the source system in this case, but there is something to be said about sticking to a pattern. It also allows you to manage the 2nd SPs ACLs independently of the runner which is helpful.

All that said, I am still a bit wary of the level of auth being provided to that SP that has access to Databricks. I don't like the idea of it having any broad write style permissions, even on the workspace. Seems risky and would be something that would draw attention in the cyber world if they were to catch wind.

Basically, if that SP has workspace admin, then it can run other jobs and gain access to the secrets that the other SPs have access to.

I'm also curious how you are able to get all the information you need when each SP is only scoped to a single workspace? or are you thinking an job runs in prod but is attached to an SP that has workspace rights on all workspaces?

*Scott*

Ok, this sounds like a good pattern (if super freakin' involved - lol).

I share your concerns regarding access. I don't think that the SP that queries the API (or, as DB prefers, uses the Python SDK) would need Workspace Admin permissions because it doesn't need to write anything to the API, it just needs to read data.

I haven't found any information on how to set scopes (not Secret Scopes) through either the API or the SDK, so I am thinking that since the SDK authenticates using OAuth, it might restrict access based on what the SP is permissioned on. That said, to list all groups and read their entitlements, maybe that does require Workspace Admin access. I honestly don't know.

*Zach*

ya permissions will be what the SP has been assigned in that case

it will just depend on the entitlements needed to get that data

*Scott*

Ok, confirmed. What SP is calling the API needs to be a workspace admin to get the necessary entitlement and membership info.

*Zach*

hmm. ok. that's not ideal. we will need to review  the data you are trying to access before it leaves PoC and see if there is another way to get you the same information without that level of access.

otherwise we'll get yelled at by cyber security and lose all the good will we have built up over the last year.

*Zach*

Yeah. It seems like the workspace entitlements data isn't available anywhere else.

So, one thing we could potentially do...I know that the way we have defined "Workspace Admin" groups includes a ton of emergency data access. But this SP doesn't need ANY data access. They just need to be part of the "admins" group for their workspace. Now, that obviously gives them some power, but I don't think that it gives them the ability to do things like create clusters and on it's own it doesn't give them any data access.

It's less privilege than the CI/CD SP, which already has admin rights.

I want to restructure the silver query for group entitlements to yield a narrow and long table that I can scan quickly and compare to a known result set.

Here's my final draft SQL query that I want to incorporate into my notebook:

WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(`id` AS LONG) AS `id`,
    displayName AS `name`,
    meta['resourceType'] AS `type`,
    CAST(get(groups, 0)['value'] AS LONG) AS `parent_id`,
    get(groups, 0)['display'] AS `parent_name`,
    e.value AS `entitlement`
  FROM
    keyera_enterprise_dev.admin.bronze_iam_group_entitlements
    LATERAL VIEW OUTER explode(entitlements) AS e
  WHERE
    get(groups, 0)['value'] IS NULL
  UNION
  SELECT
    CAST(m.value AS LONG) AS `id`,
    m.display AS `name`,
    `type`,
    CAST(id AS LONG) AS `parent_id`,
    name AS `parent_name`,
    `entitlement`
  FROM
    (
      SELECT
        `id`,
        displayName AS `name`,
        meta['resourceType'] AS `type`,
        e.value AS `entitlement`,
        members
      FROM
        keyera_enterprise_dev.admin.bronze_iam_group_entitlements
        LATERAL VIEW OUTER explode(entitlements) AS e
    ) t
    LATERAL VIEW OUTER explode(members) AS m
  WHERE
    m.`$ref` RLIKE 'Groups'
),
admin_ids AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    id
  FROM
    base
  WHERE
    name = 'admins'
    OR parent_name = 'admins'
),
final_set AS (
  SELECT
    `id`,
    `name`,
    `type`,
    `parent_id`,
    `parent_name`,
    `entitlement`
  FROM
    base
  UNION
  SELECT
    b.id AS `id`,
    b.name AS `name`,
    b.type AS `type`,
    b.parent_id AS `parent_id`,
    b.parent_name AS `parent_name`,
    'workspace-admin' AS `entitlement`
  FROM
    base b
      JOIN admin_ids a
        ON a.id = b.id
)
SELECT
  *
FROM
  final_set
ORDER BY
  `id` ASC

*ISSUE*: 

Maximo datetime (well any SQL database) has no timezone info.  

{noformat}2024-11-29 13:01:56.180{noformat}

Databricks is presenting datetimeoffset with timezone – currently the +0:00 would be inccorect representation of the same record

{noformat}2024-11-29T13:01:56.180+00:00{noformat}

POSSIBLE SOLUTIONS:

* in databricks store it as the same datatype, datetime (no timezone)
** {{2024-11-29 13:01:56.180}}
** PRO: ez to use its cgy time

Stories and tasks related to platform administration, auditing, etc.

h1. Platform Administration Items

* Complete implementation of Terraform for IaC (Infrastructure-as-Code) deployment
** Terraform is used with Databricks to define and deploy our workspaces, data catalogs, business domain data schemas, primary service principals, groups, all-purpose compute, compute policies, SQL warehouses, and to apply security permissions to all of the above.
* Transition AWS Configuration to Terraform
** Similar to Databricks, Terraform can be used with AWS to define and deploy resources as IaC. We should be using this to deploy the underlying S3 storage, virtual private clusters, and virtual private network assets for our Databricks environments.
* IAM Validation
** Databricks includes the ability to define groups, users, and service principals with fine-grained access permissions. However, it lacks built-in tools to effectively manage these objects and permissions, 
** This is a collection of notebooks, jobs, tables, and dashboards intended to validate that our system’s groups, users, and service principals, and their associated security permissions, conform to our expected state (as defined in the Terraform above). These will allow us to 1. validate that the Terraform configuration is correct, 2. detect whether any changes have been made since a Terraform deployment (either by jobs or manually), and 3. maintain a history of our IAM posture, which will improve our ability to audit access and investigate any issues.
* Auditing Scripts
** Databricks includes robust logging of almost all system events and writes those logs to system tables. However, it does not have built-in tools to analyze those logs and surface potentially concerning items. It also does not maintain this history for more than 1 year.
** This will be a library of scripts that will define potentially concerning activity, parse the system logs, and flag any items that we specify. We can also use this code base to store relevant audit logs within our own AWS storage, ensuring that we meet Keyera’s data retention policies.
* Implement DR, Backup, and Archival Patterns
** We need to define and implement our disaster recovery, source data backup, and result data archival patterns.
** This needs to include DR plans for IaC code, ETL code, virtual infrastructure fail-over, and backup of S3.
* Unification of Ingestion Patterns (potential)
** We currently use multiple patterns for ingestion of data from source systems (e.g., SQL CDC, DMS CDC, direct query, API query). This is not necessarily an issue and is – to some extent – unavoidable. However, it does increase complexity and may also increase costs. We should consider future work to normalize our ingestion patterns, where and when it makes sense.
* Decommissioning of Commercial Solutions Workspaces
** The Commercial Solutions workspaces were created as part of a separate Databricks pilot conducted with Arcurve. It has always been the plan to decommission these workspaces and merge their content into the Data Extraction and Analytics Lakehouse workspaces. This will free up workspace quota, reduce cost, and dramatically simplify system management.
* Integration of all ETL into Primary Code Base
** At present there are multiple distinct code bases handling ETL tasks: keyera-databricks, keyera-emissions, keyera-measurement, and (to a lesser extent) databricks-admin. We should consolidate all ETL code into a single code base to improve maintainability, transparency, and control.
* Configuration of Power BI as Presentation Layer
** We need to more fully investigate and possibly configure Power BI since the business uses it as their preferred presentation layer.
* Implementation of Automated Code Documentation
** Our code is documented with docstrings and readme files. We should investigate and implement an automated documentation system to consolidate and publish this technical documentation.

Here is the link to the official documentation from Energy Aspects: [Quickstart Guide|https://developer.energyaspects.com/reference/quickstart-guide]

All requests to the Data Service API require an API key. These are 16-character strings that look like {{LqTWU4gsV7tLEt7e}}. The key is provided in an "api_key" query parameter as part of your request. We have already generated an API key, which is stored in the notebook.

To get a list of all available timeseries datasets, the request is as below: [https://api.energyaspects.com/data/datasets/timeseries?api_key={YOUR_API_KEY}|https://api.energyaspects.com/data/datasets/timeseries?api_key=%7BYOUR_API_KEY%7D]

This will give you basic information about each dataset, including its dataset_id, description, source and whether or not you are licensed to retrieve its data.



*API Endpoints*

JSON
[https://api.energyaspects.com/data/timeseries/json?dataset_id={dataset_id}&api_key=|https://api.energyaspects.com/data/timeseries/json?dataset_id=%7Bdataset_id%7D&api_key=d9f3d75c-00a9-4202-b563-149dd050b2a5][{api_key}|https://api.energyaspects.com/data/timeseries/csv?dataset_id=%7Bdataset_id%7D&date_from=%7Bdate_from%7D&date_to=%7Bdate_to%7D&api_key=%7Bapi_key%7D]

CSV

·         Dependencies and scheduling are aligned with the existing pipeline cadence.

# Error Handling & Logging

·         Standardized logging is implemented.

·         Error handling and alerts are configured for failure scenarios.

# Validation

·         Test run confirms expected data output with no data loss or duplication.

# Documentation

·         The notebook is documented (purpose, inputs/outputs, assumptions).

·         Updates are made to the data pipeline description

	)

where ponum in (select distinct ponum from #key_restrict_polist)

where ponum in (select distinct ponum from #key_restrict_polist)

update invoicecost set unitcost=1, linecost=1,quantity=1

where invoicenum in (
	select distinct invoicenum from invoice where ponum in (select distinct ponum from #key_restrict_polist)

	select distinct invoicenum from invoiceline where ponum in (select distinct ponum from #key_restrict_polist)

h1. OS BD

h2. Background

OS BD Team requires an all-encompassing report that summarizes its performance in relation to customers volume with the FSCS product system. The OS BD team requires eONE data to:

# Track customer volumes and revenue to improve strategy/commercial relations
# Prepare annual budgets, 5-year forecasts, expected volumes, expected revenues
# Access/visibility to daily volumetric data to track production against the budget/plan 

h2. Request

Data examples are stored in the ‘Oilsands Data Integration Breakdown’ shared with Melanie, Gladys, and Lee. Data table requests listed by priority and accessibility: 

eONE:

# ‘Keyera Account Journal Qbyte Detail’ ingestion – this report provides key financial information based on the contracted volumes OS customers are receiving monthly. The table also has key columns (Resp cost Center Qbyte) to connect eONE data to the Qbyte system, allowing an in-depth analysis on asset performance margins.
# ‘Product Inventory” Workflow ingestion – provides further breakdown on the customer contracts, providing nuances to each individual contract additional fees or make up rights that is not represented in the rolled-up Account Journal. Key items provide OS BD with intel on opportunities to increase fees, improving revenue.
# ‘C5 Daily Balance’ (unable to source as it sits on the logistics side) - is an excel logistics manually fills in and inputs into eONE with volumes by customer by receipt/delivery point. This data would be the key for strategic planning as it will provide BD with knowledge of the upstream supply Keyera is currently capturing (market capture).  



h2. Definition of Done 

* Quality volume and financial data from eONE, Qbyte and MMs/QQ 
* Be able to identify but not limited to the 14 receipt points and 7 delivery points in eONE and MMs/QQ (MMS 75% verified) 
* Validate customer specific data including volumes flowing through each receipt/delivery point (eONE from the logistics side) 
* QA/QC with accounting reports 
* Access to the required data to prepare: 
** Power Bi dashboard – includes identification of volume flows by customer, revenue by customer and OPEX  
** Annual budgets 
** Gross OPEX 
** Operating Margin 
** 5 year forecast 
** Expected volumes 
** Expected costs (by month) 
** Capital project costs 
** Ability to measure monthly customer volumes  
** Report on profit vs. spend 
** Ability to link volume flow to contract fee for Keyera Corp. 

h2. Data Products

# Summarized Operations Data Extract 
# LI Customer Operations 
# KPLI – Keyera Account Journal QByte Detail report

h1. Logistics

h2. Background

The Logistics team currently uses a Power BI report called “Daily Facility Balance” to monitor daily storage volumes by commodity and customer. The current process for data ingestion is a three-step workflow: 

# Schedulers manually input the data into eOne. 
# IT has set up an automated export of the eOne report, which is sent to the Logistics service account mailbox in CSV format. 
# A Power Automate flow uploads the CSV to a SharePoint folder, from which Power BI pulls the data. 

While functional, this process is manual and prone to delay. We're now looking to leverage Databricks to streamline data access and automate the flow of KFS Frac & Storage Facility volumetric data into a historical dataset. The goal is to create a more efficient, scalable, and automated reporting pipeline.

h2. Request

Please refer to the attached [file: “Previou|file: “Previo]s Two Month – Facility Balance Detail.” 

* eOne Data Access: We have an existing eOne report set up, though the exact report name is still TBD. 
* Data Scope Request: Currently, we only receive data for the previous two months, which we then manually merge with historical records. We’re requesting access to a complete master table that includes all past days’ data, starting from September 2024. This would eliminate manual merging and ensure full historical visibility in Power BI.

h2. Definition of Done

* We have full access to historical data going back to September 2024. 
* Quality metrics are accurate by owner, counterparty, and location. These will be validated with the rail and truck teams once the data is complete. 
* Power BI is successfully connected to the data source. 
* Data is refreshed daily (with a one-day lag) and is available by 10 AM each day.

|Order|A list of orders for product movement. An order is a request for specific product movement, detailing the loading month, number of railcars, shipper, product, facility, route, and additional parties of interest (such as care of, importer, exporter, customs broker, payor, notify party). It also includes contracts, export permits, embargo information, instructions for facilities, and Order Status|
|Order Detail|A list of shipments for each order. A shipment is a record creted in Geo for each car on the Order. Each Order Detail contains information about shipments dates (planned, scheduled, shipped), shipment status, physical railcar assigned, name of BOL file generated for the shipment|

This Jira ticket is created for getting the data from Databricks dashboard from Measurement: Production Volumes Databricks Dashboard to Excel for the end user. Following Wallena Kendericks's request that *all front-end data be accessed digitally—similar to how KFS front-end is connected to their DCS/Historian*—we have a new ask to ensure that front-end users no longer need to manually upload or download data from Databricks. This initiative is designed to streamline daily accounting, BD, and logistics processes by integrating the necessary data directly into Excel. Our goal is to build a comprehensive, digitally accessible dataset that improves efficiency and supports self-service analytics.

*Note:* We are not supporting direct querying of Databricks from Excel for non-developers. Excel should connect to a Power BI Semantic Model that draws from Databricks.

Walina Kendrick and Dean Brunce - the person to contact for additional details

This will need to go through the Intake Process for Data Foundations

column20:
As a BD rep, I need to estimate allocated customer inlet volumes and NGL components based on historical TIPS values and to-date volumes.

*Business context:* There is up to 6-week lag in posting TIPS monthly volumes. During that time, BDs have limited visibility into facility operation and customer activity. This data can be estimated using historical data from TIPS, together with up-to-date daily data from Measurements (with GEF (Gas Equivalent Factor) applied to liquid volumes).

*Technical Details:*

The data must be presented to the business in the following columns:

||*#*||*Name*||*Description and logic*||
|1|plant_no|Unique plant_no from Posted Volumes.
For the purpose of this story, apply filters to limit the data to SIMPT and WAPTT only.|
|2|Projection From Date|# In the Posted Volumes table, for that plant_no (column 1), find the latest production month (PROD_DT).
# Set the Projection From Date to be the 1st of the month after the latest production month.|
|3|Projection To Date|Current date - 1 day.|
|4|meter_no|All unique combinations of *plant_no*, *meter_no*, *ctr_party_ba_no*, *ba_nm1*, and of the latest combination of *accounting_date* and *production_date* from Posted Volumes.|
|5|ctr_party_ba_no|All unique combinations of *plant_no*, *meter_no*, *ctr_party_ba_no*, *ba_nm1*, and of the latest combination of *accounting_date* and *production_date* from Posted Volumes.|
|6|BA_NM1|All unique combinations of *plant_no*, *meter_no*, *ctr_party_ba_no*, *ba_nm1*, and of the latest combination of *accounting_date* and *production_date* from Posted Volumes.|
|7|q2_tag_id|For *meter_no* (column 4), in the {{tips_q2_meter_mapping}}, find the *Q2 tag ID* for that meter.|
|8|MTD_INLET_VOLUME|For the Q2_tag, in {{gold_volumetrics.daily_flow_weighted_volumes}}, add up all *volume_m3* values for a time period between Projection From and Projection To dates.|
|9|CUSTOMER_SHARE_PRIOR_1_PERIOD|For *ctr_party_ba_no* and *meter_no*, in keyera_enterprise_prod.gold_tips.customer_volume_historical_proportions, find *customer_share_of_inlet_percent*.|
|10|MTD_INLET_CUSTOMER_VOLUME|Multiply MTD_INLET_VOLUME*CUSTOMER_SHARE_PRIOR_1_PERIOD.|
|11|CUSTOMER_SHARE_C2_PRIOR_1_PERIOD|For a *ctr_party_ba_no* and *meter_no*, in keyera_enterprise_prod.gold_tips.customer_volume_historical_proportions, find *ethane_c2_yield_percent*.|
|12|ETHANE_C2_VOL_PROJ_PRIOR_1_PERIOD|# For the Q2_tag, in {{gold_volumetrics.daily_flow_weighted_volumes}}, add up all the values of *c2_vol_e3m3* column for a time period between Projection From and Projection To dates.
# Multiply the calculated sum by the CUSTOMER_SHARE_PERCENT_PRIOR_1_PERIOD.|
|13|CUSTOMER_SHARE_C3_PRIOR_1_PERIOD| |
|14|ETHANE_C3_VOL_PROJ_PRIOR_1_PERIOD| |
|15| | |
|16| | |
|17| | |
| | | |

If there is a new customer or a new meter since volume posting, there will be no visibility and the data will be inaccurate.



To make a projection till ME, we need to divide the MTD volume by number of days, determine daily average and then multiply by the number of days in the month.

See full description in the metadata file (link). 

See calculations in the model file (link).

Update frequency - daily

_Use the questions below to guide business requirements. In combination with our_ [_Technical Standards_|https://keyera.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DF/pages/19104642/Technical+Standards]_, these form the functional and non-functional requirements._

* _Define_
** _What data do we think we need to solve the business problem?_
** _What other factors besides data might need to be addressed to solve the problem?_
* _Ingest_
** _What sources have the data that we think is needed?_
** _What are the characteristics of the source data that we need to be aware of (e.g., refresh cadence, quality, granularity)?_
** _Are the data sources relatively easy to access or do they require extra development to connect (e.g., is it an internal system with an accessible database, does it have an object model that makes it difficult to query, do we need to pull the data from an API and do we have access)?_
* _Transform_
** _What is the shape of the source data and what shape is needed in the final product?_
** _How clean is the source data and does it conform to Keyera standards (e.g., quality, units of measure)?_
** _Does the data need to be normalized or joined with other data sets to be useful?_
* _Process_
** _Is the source data already well understood, or does it require exploration and manipulation by a senior data analyst?_
** _Is a single set of final “gold” tables sufficient, or is there value in providing access to some intermediate date sets?_
** _How will the data be used (e.g., internal analysis, machine learning, presentation to end users)?_
* _Consume_
** _Who is the audience for the data?_
** _Does the data include sensitive or confidential information?_
** _How does the business intend to consume the data (e.g., Excel, Power BI, Databricks Dashboard, or will it feed into another system)?_

h1. Why

_What is the business problem that we are trying to solve with data?_

_A “data product” is a package of work that results in one or more related data sets that are available to data analysts and/or business consumers. Most often, a data product will require work related to definition, ingestion, transformation, processing, and consumption._

_Rather than being defined by tables in a source system, data products should be defined by deliverables that are tied to some business capability. For example:_

{quote}🚫 _“I want the data from 13 tables in Qbyte so that I can query the data for my report.”_

(/) _“I want to create a dashboard for our PMO, to support our Source-to-Pay effort by showing how cloud infrastructure costs relate to our project portfolio.”_{quote}

h3. Objective

Enable business users to access unvalidated, raw production volume data earlier in the day so they can begin working with it before MMS validation is complete. This is achieved by enhancing the existing {{gold_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes_last_fourteen_months}} table and introducing a supporting pipeline that stages and updates tag data progressively.

----

h3. Step 0: Create External Table Over AWS S3

* Define an external table named {{bronze_q2.inmation_raw_measurement_data}}.
* Point it directly to the AWS S3 bucket in the *Q2 account* where raw measurement data is stored.
* Avoid any transformations at this stage — the table should reflect the raw schema and structure of the source files.
* Ensure the table includes a {{data_load_time}} column to support downstream filtering.

h3. Step 1: Build {{silver_volumetrics.unvalidated_last_2_days}}

* Create a new table or view named {{silver_volumetrics.unvalidated_last_2_days}}.
* Source data from {{bronze_q2.inmation_raw_measurement_data}}.
* Apply a filter: {{prod_date >= current_date - 2}}.
* Add a derived column {{status}}:
** Set {{status = "UNVALIDATED"}} for all records.
* This table will serve as the authoritative source for recent unvalidated tag data and will be used in downstream logic.

h3. Step 2: Modify {{gold_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes_last_fourteen_months}}

* Update the logic of this existing table to incorporate tag data from:
** {{silver_volumetrics.unvalidated_last_2_days}} for recent unvalidated tags.
** {{silver_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes}} for MMS-validated tags.
* *Tag Source Logic by Production Date*:
** *For* {{prod_date = current_date - 2}}and beyond:
*** Use MMS data from {{silver_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes}}.
*** Use the {{status}} value provided by MMS (e.g., {{"Validated-System/Reviewed/etc"}}).
** *For* {{prod_date = current_date - 1}}:
*** Use tag data from {{silver_volumetrics.unvalidated_last_2_days}}. 
*** Use the {{status}} column already assigned in Step 1 ({{"UNVALIDATED"}}).
*** If there is a validated volume from MMS from that tag, take the MMS volume over the unvalidated tag volume.

h3. Step 3: Update Existing Job

* Modify the existing Databricks job named *Daily Production Volumes* to:
** Include logic for ingesting and processing data from {{silver_volumetrics.unvalidated_last_7_days}}.
** Run every 15 minutes between 07:00 and 09:00 local time.
** Update {{gold_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes_last_fourteen_months}} with the latest tag data and statuses.

* *Business Owner:* Tyson van Leusden
* *Business Lead:* Tania Nezic

h1. Why

_What is the business problem that we are trying to solve with data?_

_A “data product” is a package of work that results in one or more related data sets that are available to data analysts and/or business consumers. Most often, a data product will require work related to definition, ingestion, transformation, processing, and consumption._

_Rather than being defined by tables in a source system, data products should be defined by deliverables that are tied to some business capability. For example:_

{quote}🚫 _“I want the data from 13 tables in Qbyte so that I can query the data for my report.”_

(/) _“I want to create a dashboard for our PMO, to support our Source-to-Pay effort by showing how cloud infrastructure costs relate to our project portfolio.”_{quote}

h2. What is the value of solving this problem?

_What is the value of solving the problem? Wherever possible, provide a statement of tangible and quantifiable business value._

* Allows for joining measurement data to other data sets for wider usage.
* Combines measurement data with business context.
* Publishes measurement data to wider audiences.

h2. What is/isn’t the urgency tied to solving this problem?

Volumetric data is fundamental to all business lines and to enabling our analysts.

h1. How

_How will we solve this problem with data?_

* We need to provide timely access to a variety of measurement data sets, especially:
** Volumes
** Compositions
** Balancing
** Sensor Calibrations (WellTrak)
* In addition to the raw datasets, we will also make broad data available through Databricks Dashboards and via Power BI semantic models.

h1. What

_What are the specific deliverables? See the “Define” story for more on capturing requirements._

# Delivery of “raw” volume data - incorporate previous day PDAY (production day) tagged data from AWS MMS Raw data store to enable the use of daily data in nominations processes.
## Incorporation of the raw data into the Production Volumes Databricks Dashboard
## Replacement of raw data with validated data once available
# Access to balance data - so that we can streamline (and not recalculate) providing balance group data and flow weighted average sample date. (60 Day history - verify [~accountid:6230ae1375f257006a99beed])
# Delivery of curated volume data tables - the existing “gold_volumetrics” tables are too large and have variable granularity (minute, hour, day data is mixed). We must undertake data analysis and determine a set of more curated gold tables to increase usability.
# Other Compositional Data - for Measurement Quality Team Reporting & Logistics use. Includes:
## KeyeraC5+Eq
## KeyeraTraceSulphur
## KeyeraOther (Deana/Teresa)
# Access to WellTrak Data
# Translate the queries behind the Measurements Dashboard into gold tables so the curated data can be used by PA and other audiences.
# Ingest relational information (e.g., meter and sample point) from MMS PostgreSQL database.
# Possibly create component balancing table POC in sandbox - [~accountid:61d60d71a54af900697ee9aa]

Create process documentation to facilitate the integration to support the addition, update, and removal of SCIs (Service Catalog Items). * The integration process supports adding, updating, and removing SCIs in FreshService based on the content of the DUC+.

* SCI changes are logged and auditable.

* Defined SCI data model and mapping rules.

h3. *DESCRIPTION*

Enhance FreshService by establishing a standardized (as best we can) set of workflows and automations to process every Service Catalogue Item (SCI) consistently. These workflows will streamline the handling of FreshService requests and ensure that each SCI follows a predictable, auditable process from submission to fulfillment.

This enhancement supports automation, reduces manual intervention, and improves service delivery consistency.

h3. *ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA*

* A defined workflow exists for each SCI in FreshService.
* Workflows include steps such as approval routing, group assignment, and ticket resolution.
* Automations are configured to trigger based on SCI-specific criteria (e.g., product type, requester role).
* Notifications are sent to relevant stakeholders at key stages (e.g., request received, approved, fulfilled).
* Each workflow logs actions for audit purposes.
* Errors or exceptions in workflow execution are logged and surfaced to administrators.

h3. *OUT OF SCOPE*

* Manual ticket handling outside of defined workflows.
* Integration with external systems beyond FreshService (unless explicitly required by the SCI).

h3. *DEPENDENCIES*

* Access to FreshService admin console for workflow configuration.
* Complete and accurate SCI definitions.
* Defined business rules for each SCI’s fulfillment process.

h3. *NOTES*

* Consider using FreshService’s workflow automator and scenario automations for implementation.
* Align workflows with existing ITSM practices and compliance requirements.
* This enhancement lays the groundwork for scalable, automated access provisioning.

Automate the retrieval of FreshService service catalog items by configuring the Data Storefront to perform a daily GET request at 5:30 AM from FreshService. The response, a flat file containing the catalog data, will be stored in a designated folder accessible to the Data Menu for processing and display.

h3. *Acceptance Criteria*

* A scheduled job runs daily at 5:30 AM to perform a GET request to the FreshService API.
* The API call retrieves the full list of service catalog items in flat file format (JSON).
* The file is saved to a predefined folder accessible by the Data Menu.
* The job logs success/failure status and any relevant metadata (e.g., timestamp, file size).
* Errors in the API call or file write process are logged and trigger alerts.
* There is no predefined requirement for how to do the integration.

* Parsing or transforming the catalog data for display.
* Manual triggering of the job.

* FreshService API credentials and endpoint access.
* File storage location with read access for the Data Menu.
* Scheduling infrastructure (e.g., cron job, task scheduler, or cloud function).

* Authentication context to identify the current user.
* UI component library support for list rendering and empty states.

* Consider pagination or lazy loading for users with many requests.
* This feature improves transparency and reduces support inquiries by allowing users to self-verify their access requests.

As the TIPS data owner, I need to present TIPS codes with their names/descriptions to users as a Databricks table (or a set of tables) so that users can understand TIPS data and reports.

*Technical details:*

Various G&P data products use codes to identify volume types, meter types and so on. TIPS contains a separate table per code type, each table including the code itself, its description and - in most cases - the last updated time stamp. This data can be presented to users as a set of tables of a similar structure (Code, Code Description, Last Update), or as one table, with an additional column for a a code type (Code Type, Code, Code Description, Last Update). The main use of this data is to help users work with TIPS data. 

Potentially, this data can be used by other TIPS data products, for resolving codes to their names/descriptions.

As a Business Development (BD) Rep, I need to map TIPS meters to Q2 daily volume tags so that I can reconcile meter data from these two applications. 

*Business context* (optional reading)*:* 

TIPS and Q2 meters are the same physical meters, but known under different names in those applications and associated with different data elements: TIPS provides customer allocation on meters, and Q2 provides volume and composition on the same meters. Upon reconciling the meter data, BDs can estimate allocated month-to-date volumes (with composition) to customer, before these volumes are posted in TIPS. This data will be presented in [Customer Volume Projection|https://keyera.atlassian.net/browse/DF-545] table. 

*Technical context* (optional reading)*:*

For the purpose of this initiative, we only need to map the unique ID of a TIPS meter to the unique ID of the same meter in Q2. However for usability, the mapping needs to be enhanced with meter properties from each app, such as plant, product, parent device, description etc. To avoid the “garbage-in” situation, TIPS meter properties can be retrieved from the Meter Hierarchy table ({{keyera_enterprise_prod.gold_tips.meter_hierarchy}}) in Databricks. Q2 meter properties can be retrieved from MMS tables (public.measurement_tag and public.measurement_tag_suffix).

*Details:*

# Create a gold TIPS-Q2 meter mapping table in Databricks, as per product definition: [https://keyera.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DF/pages/87687169/TIPS-Q2+Meter+Mapping|https://keyera.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DF/pages/87687169/TIPS-Q2+Meter+Mapping|smart-link]. Also, there is a mock-up destination table with TIPS-Q2 data mapping here : {{keyera_temporary.sandbox.tips_q2_mapping_manual}}. Please note that the table is not exact, just a rough draft. Use the product definition in Confluence as a final reference.
# Populate the table as follows:
# Bring the key columns from silver_sharepoint_site_data_foundations.tips_q2_meter_mapping (all columns):[https://keyera.atlassian.net/browse/DF-789|https://keyera.atlassian.net/browse/DF-789|smart-link] 

* TIPS Meter #
* Q2 Tag ID
* Updated By
* Updated On

# Add TIPS meter properties to the TIPS-Q2 meter mapping table: 
For each TIPS meter #, find a records of that meter #  in {{keyera_enterprise_prod.gold_tips.meter_hierarchy}} for the most recent combination of Production Period (PROD_DT) and Accounting Period (ACCT_DT) and populate the following properties: 

* Production Period 
* Accounting Period 
* TIPS Plant Code
* TIPS Plant Name
* TIPS Parent       
* TIPS Meter #
* TIPS Product
* TIPS Plant Meter
* TIPS Meter Description
* TIPS Meter UOM

If TIPS meter # can’t be found in the meter hierarchy table, populate all the fields with “Not found in TIPS meter hierarchy”.

# Add Q2 tag properties to the TIPS-Q2 meter mapping table:
For each Q2 Tag ID, retrieve the following properties from public.measurement_tag and public.measurement_tag_suffix tables (exact mapping to be specified after [https://keyera.atlassian.net/browse/DF-688|https://keyera.atlassian.net/browse/DF-688|smart-link]  ):

* Q2 Product
* Q2 Parent Device ID
* Q2 Device Description
* Q2 UOM

If a tag can’t be found in any of the two tables, populate the fields with “Not found in Q2 tags”.



*Acceptance Criteria*

* The TIPS-Q2 meter mapping table exists in Databricks with accurate data.
* The TIPS-Q2 meter mapping table in Databricks can be updated on demand.

*Definition of Done:*

* Code is Written and Reviewed via Pull Request
* Code Passes Unit Tests
* Solution is Documented (README, docstrings, etc.).
* Terraform is Updated (to create resource dependencies like groups, Service Principals, catalogs, schemas, etc.)
* Development Deployment is Validated
* Story is Attached to a Release
* Release is Deployed to Test

h1. Benny AI Chatbot - Initial Production Deployment Plan

h2. Application Overview

Multi-region AI chatbot application with frontend in Canada and backend in Europe for data sovereignty compliance.

h2. Architecture Components

h3. Frontend (Canada - ca-central-1)

* *Nginx Load Balancer*: Routes traffic and serves static content
* *React Frontend*: User interface for chat interactions
* *Public ALB*: Internet-facing load balancer

h3. Backend (Europe - eu-central-1)

* *FastAPI Backend*: Handles chat logic and AI processing
* *Internal ALB*: Private load balancer for backend services
* *AWS Bedrock*: AI/ML inference service
* *Secrets Manager*: JWT tokens and configuration

h2. Deployment Order

h3. Phase 1: Infrastructure (Pre-deployed by SysAdmin)

* VPCs and networking (both regions)
* Security groups and VPC endpoints
* Application Load Balancers
* ECS clusters

h3. Phase 2: Container Images

# *Backend Image* (eu-central-1)
#* Build and push to ECR: {{key-benny-backend:latest}}
# *Frontend Image* (ca-central-1)
#* Build and push to ECR: {{key-benny-frontend:latest}}
# *Nginx Image* (ca-central-1)
#* Build and push to ECR: {{key-benny-nginx:latest}}

h3. Phase 3: Application Services

# *Backend Service* (eu-central-1)
#* ECS service with FastAPI backend
#* Connects to Bedrock for AI processing
#* Health check: {{/health}} endpoint
# *Frontend Services* (ca-central-1)
#* ECS service with Nginx + React frontend
#* Connects to backend in Europe
#* Health check: HTTP 200 on port 80

h3. Phase 4: DNS & Traffic

* Configure DNS to point to Canada ALB
* Verify end-to-end connectivity

h2. Key Configuration

h3. Environment Variables

* {{BACKEND_ALB_DNS}}: Internal backend endpoint
* {{AZURE_AD_METADATA_URL}}: Authentication configuration
* {{FRANKFURT_KNOWLEDGE_BASE_ID}}: Bedrock knowledge base

h3. Secrets (Stored in Secrets Manager)

* {{JWT_SECRET}}: Authentication token secret

h2. Health Checks

* *Backend*: {{http://backend-alb/health}} returns 200
* *Frontend*: {{http://frontend-alb/}} returns 200
* *End-to-end*: Chat functionality works through UI

h2. Rollback Plan

* Scale ECS services to 0 desired count
* Revert DNS if needed
* Container images remain in ECR for quick restart

h2. Estimated Deployment Time

* *Container builds*: 15-20 minutes
* *Service deployment*: 10-15 minutes
* *DNS propagation*: 2-5 minutes
* *Total*: ~30-40 minutes

We have large numbers of contracts and amendments that we need to understand and analyze in aggregate.

h1. How

_How do we propose solving this problem with data?_

h1. What

h2. Requirements

_Use the questions below to guide business requirements. In combination with our_ [_Technical Standards_|https://keyera.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DF/pages/19104642/Technical+Standards]_, these form the functional and non-functional requirements._

* Define
** What data do we think we need to solve the business problem?
** What other factors besides data might need to be addressed to solve the problem?
* Ingest
** What sources have the data that we think is needed?
** What are the characteristics of the source data that we need to be aware of (e.g., refresh cadence, quality, granularity)?
** Are the data sources relatively easy to access or do they require extra development to connect (e.g., is it an internal system with an accessible database, does it have an object model that makes it difficult to query, do we need to pull the data from an API and do we have access)?
* Transform
** What is the shape of the source data and what shape is needed in the final product?
** How clean is the source data and does it conform to Keyera standards (e.g., quality, units of measure)?
** Does the data need to be normalized or joined with other data sets to be useful?
* Process
** Is the source data already well understood, or does it require exploration and manipulation by a senior data analyst?
** Is a single set of final “gold” tables sufficient, or is there value in providing access to some intermediate date sets?
** How will the data be used (e.g., internal analysis, machine learning, presentation to end users)?
* Consume
** Who is the audience for the data?
** Does the data include sensitive or confidential information?
** How does the business intend to consume the data (e.g., Excel, Power BI, Databricks Dashboard, or will it feed into another system)?

If a column is blank at the time the table is created, the ingestion script may create the column as a numeric type even though it should be a string. ### Still clean column names. Current way works.

### Enforce null checks. e.g. if there is a null value in gas composition, set it to 0
### Enforce composite keys (scd2)

h1. What is the problem?

FCTT month end process is run manually through Excel. It starts with collecting data from Dearman, eOne and Comp Match, ensuring the sync of data across these three systems, running calculations and producing a set of customer-facing documents, and providing data on customer billing to eOne. These are manual step, time-consuming and error-prone, and includes a lot of communication and coordination of effort for Logistics, Plant Accounting and Measurements. 

This data then become input into more calculations for FCTT balancing.

Users will require an ability to re-load the data on demand (for example, after correcting data in the source system), as month-end processes are time-sensitive.

h1. What is the problem?

The business (Measurements) requires regular access (several times a day) to Comp Match data. Due to the residency of this data in the OT network, the access needs to be facilitated by IT. This state implies constant dependency of business users on IT resources, for whom this work is mostly a disruption. Additionally, passing the results to the business relies on multiple manual steps, such as running data queries, entering query parameters, copying and pasting data, which is error-prone. Any errors can have significant financial and reputational cost to Keyera.

h2. What is the value of resolving this problem?

Providing business users with access to this data through Databricks can resolve the above issues of business dependency, IT work overload and the risks associated with human errors. In addition to the Measurements group, this information is required by Logistics and BD groups.

h2. Why is/isn’t this work urgent?

Urgent for two reasons:

* Long overdue promise to the business to provide them with independent data access
* Freeing IT time, currently taken to facilitate data access for the business

h1. How will we solve it?

Dashboards with graphics and lists will be created for each data set that is currently generated by IT for business users. Users will be provisioned with access to the dashboards, some with limited view-only access, others (early adopters) - with ability to create their own dashboards.

_Melissa M updated this epic description on 2025-06-04. The older version of this epic has been moved to comments below._

+*Background/Overview*+

* The G&P BD team needs access to the TIPS posted volumes data for the following reasons:
** To see what our customers see. The QQ data provides information about what is being delivered to the plant, but the values are not allocated to customers and the NGL components are not broken out. Having this data will allows us to go into customer conversations with all the info they have and identify issues at the plant or with customer sooner. 
** Projection of TIPS data on to QQ volumes to estimate NGL components and customer volumes prior to the monthly TIPS data being posted. There is an approximately 6-week lag between the prior period data and current day. Tracking the customers volumes and NGL components are important for pipeline nominations and customer relations. 
* This is multi-step request that will need to be completed for Simonette and Wapiti before moving on the South G&P facilities. 

+*Request*+

Workflow is outlined in the _BD Customer Working Volume Projection_ excel file (Lee and Melissa built this workflow in excel to be a guide for the process to be built in Databricks). The steps are generally:

# Pull data from TIPS using the “Pull Allocated Volumes Posted 2” query (attached). This work is in progress (link to Jira) 
# Recreate the table in the _Customer WI for Posted_ _Periods_ tab in the _BD Customer Working Volume Projection_ excel file. Make this a gold table. 
#* The purpose of this table is to sum the relevant components from the TIPS Posted Volumes table by customer and month. Additionally, NGL yields are calculated (volume of NGL/total inlet * 100%)
# Recreate the _BD Customer Working Volume Proj_ tab in the _BD Customer Working Volume Projection_ excel file.
#* The purpose of this table is to calculate the historical proportion of the customer's volume at the TIPS meter and the NGL yields. The historical proportions are averaged over a 1-, 3- and 6-month period so that analysis can be adjusted.  
#* This table does not need to be published as a gold table, but will be used for subsequent steps of this analysis. 
# Map/connect TIP meters to QQ meters. Example of this work was completed by Gladys/Melissa in the _Meter Mapping_ tab. 
#* The purpose of this table is to connect TIPS and QQ data.
# Recreate the _Customer Work Vol. Projections_ tab. 
#* The purpose of this data is to have an estimate of what the allocated customer inlet volume and NGL components will be based on the historical TIPS values. This will give us insight into facility operations and customer activity prior to receiving the Posted Volumes from TIPS (~6-week lag in data currently).  

+*Desired Outcome:*+

#  Gold table for Wapiti and Simonette (single table for both facilities) containing columns on the _Customer WI for Posted_ _Periods_ tab of the _BD Customer Working Volume Projection_ excel file.
# Access to the data calculated in steps 4 and 5 above.

h1. What is the problem?

The business wants to expand reporting on emissions by building on the work done for Rimbey and expanding it to Wapiti. An in-person session at Wapiti on May 28th provides an excellent opportunity to share data the project’s work on emissions data automation with the broader organization.

Our roll out of the Rimbey and Wapiti emissions data dashboard will follow a few months of successful quantification and replication of compliance calculations.

h2. What is the value to the business if we solve this problem?

We will use the dashboards for accruals going forward, and give access to select operations personnel. Operations will be able to use near-real-time emissions metrics to run tests and pilots on efficiency and emissions reduction projects, and to make quick and informed data driven decisions. The dashboards provide more granularity for operations and supporting groups, which will continue supporting Rimbey, Wapiti, and other facilities in identifying new opportunities for more efficient operation.

This will also allow us to decommission our existing time consuming, Excel-based calculators; it will also allow us to cancel contracts with Envirosoft, as we will no longer need to replicate emissions estimates to prove their reliability for compliance.

h2. Why is/isn’t this work urgent?

This work follows on from the Rimbey emissions pilot. It is necessary to get us closer to a clear and timely picture of our emissions and related costs.

h1. How will we solve it?

Add Wapiti data into the current emissions dashboard for automation of emissions metrics with required workflows to be presented on May 28th at Wapiti site to Operations, Maintenance, BD and Ops T teams. Two new emissions calculation workflows are new to Wapiti and need to be developed into the existing pipeline:

* ABGPI Workflow
* Venting Workflow

Further, emissions calculations already previously developed for Rimbey will be reused for Wapiti. These include: 

* Fuel Gas Combustion emissions
* Electrical emissions
* Fugitive emissions
* Flaring emissions
* Liquid Fuel emissions

This will require validating and adding business metadata into Unity Catalog.

For this data product, the following access will be provisioned:

# Business User Access Package (for the Sustainability Team)

h1. Overview

Schedulers (Derek Kam) complete a daily upload of raw meter volumes into EnergySys to support daily scheduling and monthly actualization.

h1. As-Is

Schedulers receive data by email from Field Measure Coordinators and enter the data into a spreadsheet. There are typically 19 records per day with fewer than 10 fields. The primary key for the data is a Meter ID field, with data following the pattern “FIT-#####”. Multiple days of records may be imported at one time. The scheduler uploads the data to EnergySys using the I 9999 workbook, and the data is populated into the Daily Raw Meter Volumes table.

An example of the existing data import worksheet has been attached to this story.

h1. To-Be

Each day, data for the previous day will be extracted from the {{keyera_measurement_prod.gold_volumetrics.final_measurement_data}} table, cleaned and processed by a notebook, and saved to a .csv file in a SharePoint location. The EnergySys file connector will watch for the file and complete the import using the existing I 9999 process. Email notifications with attached .csv files will be sent to the schedulers at each step in the process as a manual check, but manual intervention will not be required to complete the process. Email notifications must be configurable so that they can be turned off or directed to different recipients.

A sample query structure (SQL) has been attached to this story.

*Note:* Further validation of both the query and its outputs should be completed before notebook development starts.

h1. Other Considerations

This may be a good time to restructure the catalogs and schemas holding volumetric data from MMS. [Manage scheduled dashboard updates and subscriptions | Databricks on AWS|https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dashboards/schedule-subscribe]

I need to define Service Principals to run workspace admin tasks in each workspace, as well as an SP in each workspace that can be provisioned with both “workspace admin” access and API credentials to the Workspace API. This will be used to query the API and can information on workspace configuration and entitlements.

Below is an excerpt from a conversation with Zach:

Scott

Hey, got a question for you:

I have code that uses the Databricks Python SDK to query the Workspace API. In order to that, it defaults to authenticating to the API using the identity of the Service Principal that's running the job; however, I could pass in different credentials (using DB secrets) if I wanted to. Whichever SP I use has to be permissioned with access to the API.

 Do you think it would make more sense to:

  1. Permission each global STL runner SP against the API for their particular workspace
  2. Create a specific SP for each workspace whose credentials I explicitly invoke to query the API
  3. Create a different SP other than the Global STL Runner to run these specific jobs
  4. Something else I haven't thought of

?

Zach

hmm. let me think about that. need to consider where the risk sits in each case under a breach. options 2 and 3 are the same under Keyera's current security requirements.

so its a decision between does the ETL runner SP get access to the API or does a separte SP

Ok so if we are going to follow the general pattern it will be a combination of 1 and 2.

First off there is a different SP runner for every source system. the global one is only used for gold. So you will have a SP Extraction Databricks | <workspace> service principal. That SP then has the ACLs for read access on the secret scope that stores the credentials for accessing the source application. The credentials would then be tied to a different databricks SP.

Now the second SP seems redundant b/c Databricks is the source system in this case, but there is something to be said about sticking to a pattern. It also allows you to manage the 2nd SPs ACLs independently of the runner which is helpful.

All that said, I am still a bit wary of the level of auth being provided to that SP that has access to Databricks. I don't like the idea of it having any broad write style permissions, even on the workspace. Seems risky and would be something that would draw attention in the cyber world if they were to catch wind.

Basically, if that SP has workspace admin, then it can run other jobs and gain access to the secrets that the other SPs have access to.

I'm also curious how you are able to get all the information you need when each SP is only scoped to a single workspace? or are you thinking an job runs in prod but is attached to an SP that has workspace rights on all workspaces?

Scott

Ok, this sounds like a good pattern (if super freakin' involved - lol).

I share your concerns regarding access. I don't think that the SP that queries the API (or, as DB prefers, uses the Python SDK) would need Workspace Admin permissions because it doesn't need to write anything to the API, it just needs to read data.

I haven't found any information on how to set scopes (not Secret Scopes) through either the API or the SDK, so I am thinking that since the SDK authenticates using OAuth, it might restrict access based on what the SP is permissioned on. That said, to list all groups and read their entitlements, maybe that does require Workspace Admin access. I honestly don't know.

Zach

ya permissions will be what the SP has been assigned in that case

it will just depend on the entitlements needed to get that data

Scott

Ok, confirmed. What SP is calling the API needs to be a workspace admin to get the necessary entitlement and membership info.

Zach

hmm. ok. that's not ideal. we will need to review  the data you are trying to access before it leaves PoC and see if there is another way to get you the same information without that level of access.

otherwise we'll get yelled at by cyber security and lose all the good will we have built up over the last year.

Zach

Yeah. It seems like the workspace entitlements data isn't available anywhere else.

So, one thing we could potentially do...I know that the way we have defined "Workspace Admin" groups includes a ton of emergency data access. But this SP doesn't need ANY data access. They just need to be part of the "admins" group for their workspace. Now, that obviously gives them some power, but I don't think that it gives them the ability to do things like create clusters and on it's own it doesn't give them any data access.

It's less privilege than the CI/CD SP, which already has admin rights.

Stories and tasks related to platform administration, auditing, etc.

Platform Administration Items

  • Complete implementation of Terraform for IaC (Infrastructure-as-Code) deployment
    • Terraform is used with Databricks to define and deploy our workspaces, data catalogs, business domain data schemas, primary service principals, groups, all-purpose compute, compute policies, SQL warehouses, and to apply security permissions to all of the above.
  • Transition AWS Configuration to Terraform
    • Similar to Databricks, Terraform can be used with AWS to define and deploy resources as IaC. We should be using this to deploy the underlying S3 storage, virtual private clusters, and virtual private network assets for our Databricks environments.
  • IAM Validation
    • Databricks includes the ability to define groups, users, and service principals with fine-grained access permissions. However, it lacks built-in tools to effectively manage these objects and permissions,
    • This is a collection of notebooks, jobs, tables, and dashboards intended to validate that our system’s groups, users, and service principals, and their associated security permissions, conform to our expected state (as defined in the Terraform above). These will allow us to 1. validate that the Terraform configuration is correct, 2. detect whether any changes have been made since a Terraform deployment (either by jobs or manually), and 3. maintain a history of our IAM posture, which will improve our ability to audit access and investigate any issues.
  • Auditing Scripts
    • Databricks includes robust logging of almost all system events and writes those logs to system tables. However, it does not have built-in tools to analyze those logs and surface potentially concerning items. It also does not maintain this history for more than 1 year.
    • This will be a library of scripts that will define potentially concerning activity, parse the system logs, and flag any items that we specify. We can also use this code base to store relevant audit logs within our own AWS storage, ensuring that we meet Keyera’s data retention policies.
  • Implement DR, Backup, and Archival Patterns
    • We need to define and implement our disaster recovery, source data backup, and result data archival patterns.
    • This needs to include DR plans for IaC code, ETL code, virtual infrastructure fail-over, and backup of S3.
  • Unification of Ingestion Patterns (potential)
    • We currently use multiple patterns for ingestion of data from source systems (e.g., SQL CDC, DMS CDC, direct query, API query). This is not necessarily an issue and is – to some extent – unavoidable. However, it does increase complexity and may also increase costs. We should consider future work to normalize our ingestion patterns, where and when it makes sense.
  • Decommissioning of Commercial Solutions Workspaces
    • The Commercial Solutions workspaces were created as part of a separate Databricks pilot conducted with Arcurve. It has always been the plan to decommission these workspaces and merge their content into the Data Extraction and Analytics Lakehouse workspaces. This will free up workspace quota, reduce cost, and dramatically simplify system management.
  • Integration of all ETL into Primary Code Base
    • At present there are multiple distinct code bases handling ETL tasks: keyera-databricks, keyera-emissions, keyera-measurement, and (to a lesser extent) databricks-admin. We should consolidate all ETL code into a single code base to improve maintainability, transparency, and control.
  • Configuration of Power BI as Presentation Layer
    • We need to more fully investigate and possibly configure Power BI since the business uses it as their preferred presentation layer.
  • Implementation of Automated Code Documentation
    • Our code is documented with docstrings and readme files. We should investigate and implement an automated documentation system to consolidate and publish this technical documentation.

column20:
OS BD

Background

OS BD Team requires an all-encompassing report that summarizes its performance in relation to customers volume with the FSCS product system. The OS BD team requires eONE data to:

  1. Track customer volumes and revenue to improve strategy/commercial relations
  2. Prepare annual budgets, 5-year forecasts, expected volumes, expected revenues
  3. Access/visibility to daily volumetric data to track production against the budget/plan 

Request

Data examples are stored in the ‘Oilsands Data Integration Breakdown’ shared with Melanie, Gladys, and Lee. Data table requests listed by priority and accessibility: 

eONE:

  1. ‘Keyera Account Journal Qbyte Detail’ ingestion – this report provides key financial information based on the contracted volumes OS customers are receiving monthly. The table also has key columns (Resp cost Center Qbyte) to connect eONE data to the Qbyte system, allowing an in-depth analysis on asset performance margins.
  2. ‘Product Inventory” Workflow ingestion – provides further breakdown on the customer contracts, providing nuances to each individual contract additional fees or make up rights that is not represented in the rolled-up Account Journal. Key items provide OS BD with intel on opportunities to increase fees, improving revenue.
  3. ‘C5 Daily Balance’ (unable to source as it sits on the logistics side) - is an excel logistics manually fills in and inputs into eONE with volumes by customer by receipt/delivery point. This data would be the key for strategic planning as it will provide BD with knowledge of the upstream supply Keyera is currently capturing (market capture).  

Definition of Done 

  • Quality volume and financial data from eONE, Qbyte and MMs/QQ 
  • Be able to identify but not limited to the 14 receipt points and 7 delivery points in eONE and MMs/QQ (MMS 75% verified) 
  • Validate customer specific data including volumes flowing through each receipt/delivery point (eONE from the logistics side) 
  • QA/QC with accounting reports 
  • Access to the required data to prepare: 
    • Power Bi dashboard – includes identification of volume flows by customer, revenue by customer and OPEX  
    • Annual budgets 
    • Gross OPEX 
    • Operating Margin 
    • 5 year forecast 
    • Expected volumes 
    • Expected costs (by month) 
    • Capital project costs 
    • Ability to measure monthly customer volumes  
    • Report on profit vs. spend 
    • Ability to link volume flow to contract fee for Keyera Corp. 

Data Products

  1. Summarized Operations Data Extract 
  2. LI Customer Operations 
  3. KPLI – Keyera Account Journal QByte Detail report

Logistics

Background

The Logistics team currently uses a Power BI report called “Daily Facility Balance” to monitor daily storage volumes by commodity and customer. The current process for data ingestion is a three-step workflow: 

  1. Schedulers manually input the data into eOne. 
  2. IT has set up an automated export of the eOne report, which is sent to the Logistics service account mailbox in CSV format. 
  3. A Power Automate flow uploads the CSV to a SharePoint folder, from which Power BI pulls the data. 

While functional, this process is manual and prone to delay. We're now looking to leverage Databricks to streamline data access and automate the flow of KFS Frac & Storage Facility volumetric data into a historical dataset. The goal is to create a more efficient, scalable, and automated reporting pipeline.

Request

Please refer to the attached file: “Previous Two Month – Facility Balance Detail.” 

  • eOne Data Access: We have an existing eOne report set up, though the exact report name is still TBD.
  • Data Scope Request: Currently, we only receive data for the previous two months, which we then manually merge with historical records. We’re requesting access to a complete master table that includes all past days’ data, starting from September 2024. This would eliminate manual merging and ensure full historical visibility in Power BI.

Definition of Done

  • We have full access to historical data going back to September 2024. 
  • Quality metrics are accurate by owner, counterparty, and location. These will be validated with the rail and truck teams once the data is complete. 
  • Power BI is successfully connected to the data source. 
  • Data is refreshed daily (with a one-day lag) and is available by 10 AM each day.

column20:
As a BD rep, I need to estimate allocated customer inlet volumes and NGL components based on historical TIPS values and to-date volumes.

Business context: There is up to 6-week lag in posting TIPS monthly volumes. During that time, BDs have limited visibility into facility operation and customer activity. This data can be estimated using historical data from TIPS, together with up-to-date daily data from Measurements (with GEF (Gas Equivalent Factor) applied to liquid volumes).

Technical Details:

The data must be presented to the business in the following columns:

# Name Description and logic
1 plant_no Unique plant_no from Posted Volumes.
For the purpose of this story, apply filters to limit the data to SIMPT and WAPTT only.
2 Projection From Date
  1. In the Posted Volumes table, for that plant_no (column 1), find the latest production month (PROD_DT).
  2. Set the Projection From Date to be the 1st of the month after the latest production month.
3 Projection To Date Current date - 1 day.
4 meter_no All unique combinations of plant_no, meter_no, ctr_party_ba_no, ba_nm1, and of the latest combination of accounting_date and production_date from Posted Volumes.
5 ctr_party_ba_no All unique combinations of plant_no, meter_no, ctr_party_ba_no, ba_nm1, and of the latest combination of accounting_date and production_date from Posted Volumes.
6 BA_NM1 All unique combinations of plant_no, meter_no, ctr_party_ba_no, ba_nm1, and of the latest combination of accounting_date and production_date from Posted Volumes.
7 q2_tag_id For meter_no (column 4), in the tips_q2_meter_mapping, find the Q2 tag ID for that meter.
8 MTD_INLET_VOLUME For the Q2_tag, in gold_volumetrics.daily_flow_weighted_volumes, add up all volume_m3 values for a time period between Projection From and Projection To dates.
9 CUSTOMER_SHARE_PRIOR_1_PERIOD For ctr_party_ba_no and meter_no, in keyera_enterprise_prod.gold_tips.customer_volume_historical_proportions, find customer_share_of_inlet_percent.
10 MTD_INLET_CUSTOMER_VOLUME Multiply MTD_INLET_VOLUME*CUSTOMER_SHARE_PRIOR_1_PERIOD.
11 CUSTOMER_SHARE_C2_PRIOR_1_PERIOD For a ctr_party_ba_no and meter_no, in keyera_enterprise_prod.gold_tips.customer_volume_historical_proportions, find ethane_c2_yield_percent.
12 ETHANE_C2_VOL_PROJ_PRIOR_1_PERIOD
  1. For the Q2_tag, in gold_volumetrics.daily_flow_weighted_volumes, add up all the values of c2_vol_e3m3 column for a time period between Projection From and Projection To dates.
  2. Multiply the calculated sum by the CUSTOMER_SHARE_PERCENT_PRIOR_1_PERIOD.
13 CUSTOMER_SHARE_C3_PRIOR_1_PERIOD  
14 ETHANE_C3_VOL_PROJ_PRIOR_1_PERIOD  
15    
16    
17    
     

If there is a new customer or a new meter since volume posting, there will be no visibility and the data will be inaccurate.

To make a projection till ME, we need to divide the MTD volume by number of days, determine daily average and then multiply by the number of days in the month.

Tasks related to provisioning data analyst access to a given data product are grouped into a “Business User Access Package.” The intention is to ensure that the business is equipped to quickly and easily take advantage of every new data product delivered. See the project Technical Standards for more information.

  1. Create a single internal, developer APP AD group (e.g., SG_ALL_IT_DF_<business_team_abbrv>ALL_APPS_DEVELOPER<IN|CF>) to secure the PowerBI workspace, the compute clusters, and the writable unity catalog location.
    1. Note: This is required per team, not per data product.
  2. Create a PowerBI workspace for the business team to publish and share visualizations created in Power BI.
  3. Create a Unity Catalog location (e.g., keyera_sandbox_<business_team>) to allows the business team to save queries, notebooks, and tables within the Databricks (Lakehouse-Production) workspace.
  4. Create required compute clusters (SQL and General Compute) specific to the business team allowing read and write, attached to the appropriate workspace. Clusters must be tagged (at minimum) with "cost_centre" = "<business_team>". Cost policies must be applied to each cluster limiting usage to CAD $100 / day / cluster.

Ingestion covers connecting to source systems, creating bronze tables and extracting data into those tables, cleaning the data, and loading it into silver tables. Note: It does not include the application of business logic or the creation of gold tables.

Please provide a description of the source systems and the tables that will be ingested, along with any technical requirements. If the Data Product requires more than one source system or requires multiple steps to connect and stage the data, we may need to create more than one story. Use the questions below to guide your work.

  • What source systems are we ingesting from?
  • What method are we using to connect to those systems?
  • Are the data sources relatively easy to access or do they require extra development to connect (e.g., is it an internal system with an accessible database, does it have an object model that makes it difficult to query, do we need to pull the data from an API and do we have access)?
  • What is the necessary refresh cadence?
  • What is the desired ingest granularity?

Use the questions below to guide business requirements. In combination with our Technical Standards, these form the functional and non-functional requirements.

  • Define
    • What data do we think we need to solve the business problem?
    • What other factors besides data might need to be addressed to solve the problem?
  • Ingest
    • What sources have the data that we think is needed?
    • What are the characteristics of the source data that we need to be aware of (e.g., refresh cadence, quality, granularity)?
    • Are the data sources relatively easy to access or do they require extra development to connect (e.g., is it an internal system with an accessible database, does it have an object model that makes it difficult to query, do we need to pull the data from an API and do we have access)?
  • Transform
    • What is the shape of the source data and what shape is needed in the final product?
    • How clean is the source data and does it conform to Keyera standards (e.g., quality, units of measure)?
    • Does the data need to be normalized or joined with other data sets to be useful?
  • Process
    • Is the source data already well understood, or does it require exploration and manipulation by a senior data analyst?
    • Is a single set of final “gold” tables sufficient, or is there value in providing access to some intermediate date sets?
    • How will the data be used (e.g., internal analysis, machine learning, presentation to end users)?
  • Consume
    • Who is the audience for the data?
    • Does the data include sensitive or confidential information?
    • How does the business intend to consume the data (e.g., Excel, Power BI, Databricks Dashboard, or will it feed into another system)?

Objective

Enable business users to access unvalidated, raw production volume data earlier in the day so they can begin working with it before MMS validation is complete. This is achieved by enhancing the existing gold_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes_last_fourteen_months table and introducing a supporting pipeline that stages and updates tag data progressively.

Step 0: Create External Table Over AWS S3

  • Define an external table named bronze_q2.inmation_raw_measurement_data.
  • Point it directly to the AWS S3 bucket in the Q2 account where raw measurement data is stored.
  • Avoid any transformations at this stage — the table should reflect the raw schema and structure of the source files.
  • Ensure the table includes a data_load_time column to support downstream filtering.

Step 1: Build silver_volumetrics.unvalidated_last_2_days

  • Create a new table or view named silver_volumetrics.unvalidated_last_2_days.
  • Source data from bronze_q2.inmation_raw_measurement_data.
  • Apply a filter: prod_date >= current_date - 2.
  • Add a derived column status:
    • Set status = "UNVALIDATED" for all records.
  • This table will serve as the authoritative source for recent unvalidated tag data and will be used in downstream logic.

Step 2: Modify gold_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes_last_fourteen_months

  • Update the logic of this existing table to incorporate tag data from:
    • silver_volumetrics.unvalidated_last_2_days for recent unvalidated tags.
    • silver_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes for MMS-validated tags.
  • Tag Source Logic by Production Date:
    • For {{prod_date = current_date - 2}}and beyond:
      • Use MMS data from silver_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes.
      • Use the status value provided by MMS (e.g., "Validated-System/Reviewed/etc").
    • For prod_date = current_date - 1:
      • Use tag data from silver_volumetrics.unvalidated_last_2_days.
      • Use the status column already assigned in Step 1 ("UNVALIDATED").
      • If there is a validated volume from MMS from that tag, take the MMS volume over the unvalidated tag volume.

Step 3: Update Existing Job

  • Modify the existing Databricks job named Daily Production Volumes to:
    • Include logic for ingesting and processing data from silver_volumetrics.unvalidated_last_7_days.
    • Run every 15 minutes between 07:00 and 09:00 local time.
    • Update gold_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes_last_fourteen_months with the latest tag data and statuses.

    • What data do we think we need to solve the business problem?

• Business Owner: Tyson van Leusden
  • Business Lead: Tania Nezic

Why

What is the business problem that we are trying to solve with data?

A “data product” is a package of work that results in one or more related data sets that are available to data analysts and/or business consumers. Most often, a data product will require work related to definition, ingestion, transformation, processing, and consumption.

Rather than being defined by tables in a source system, data products should be defined by deliverables that are tied to some business capability. For example:

�� “I want the data from 13 tables in Qbyte so that I can query the data for my report.”

“I want to create a dashboard for our PMO, to support our Source-to-Pay effort by showing how cloud infrastructure costs relate to our project portfolio.”

What is the value of solving this problem?

What is the value of solving the problem? Wherever possible, provide a statement of tangible and quantifiable business value.

  • Allows for joining measurement data to other data sets for wider usage.
  • Combines measurement data with business context.
  • Publishes measurement data to wider audiences.

What is/isn’t the urgency tied to solving this problem?

Volumetric data is fundamental to all business lines and to enabling our analysts.

How

How will we solve this problem with data?

  • We need to provide timely access to a variety of measurement data sets, especially:
    • Volumes
    • Compositions
    • Balancing
    • Sensor Calibrations (WellTrak)
  • In addition to the raw datasets, we will also make broad data available through Databricks Dashboards and via Power BI semantic models.

What

What are the specific deliverables? See the “Define” story for more on capturing requirements.

  1. Delivery of “raw” volume data - incorporate previous day PDAY (production day) tagged data from AWS MMS Raw data store to enable the use of daily data in nominations processes.
    1. Incorporation of the raw data into the Production Volumes Databricks Dashboard
    2. Replacement of raw data with validated data once available
  2. Access to balance data - so that we can streamline (and not recalculate) providing balance group data and flow weighted average sample date. (60 Day history - verify Pauline Telan)
  3. Delivery of curated volume data tables - the existing “gold_volumetrics” tables are too large and have variable granularity (minute, hour, day data is mixed). We must undertake data analysis and determine a set of more curated gold tables to increase usability.
  4. Other Compositional Data - for Measurement Quality Team Reporting & Logistics use. Includes:
    1. KeyeraC5+Eq
    2. KeyeraTraceSulphur
    3. KeyeraOther (Deana/Teresa)
  5. Access to WellTrak Data
  6. Translate the queries behind the Measurements Dashboard into gold tables so the curated data can be used by PA and other audiences.
  7. Ingest relational information (e.g., meter and sample point) from MMS PostgreSQL database.
  8. Possibly create component balancing table POC in sandbox - Bill Wells

DESCRIPTION
Create process documentation to facilitate the integration to support the addition, update, and removal of SCIs (Service Catalog Items). This process may be automated or manual depending on the scope and complexity of the task. I would suggest we focus on manual process and convert that to an automated process should we have the resources to do so. The goal is to ensure accurate and timely synchronization of SCI data between DUC+ and FreshService to support service management workflows.

This enhancement improves data consistency and operational efficiency in configuration management.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

  • The integration process supports adding, updating, and removing SCIs in FreshService based on the content of the DUC+.
  • Manual and automated processes are clearly defined and documented.
  • SCI changes are logged and auditable.

OUT OF SCOPE

  • SCI management for systems not tracked in DUC+.
  • Enhancements to DUC+ or FreshService outside of SCI synchronization.

DEPENDENCIES

  • API or data access to DUC+ and FreshService.
  • Defined SCI data model and mapping rules.
  • Authentication and authorization for integration endpoints.

NOTES

  • Ensure compliance with Keyera’s configuration management and audit policies.
  • Include error handling and alerting for failed sync operations.
  • This enhancement lays the groundwork for broader CMDB automation.
